result:
Here is how I read your request. People who check the timetable should see a clear warning when a sailing will not run. That way they do not travel to the terminal for a ferry that will not leave.

What I found in the code:

- The Flask app reads `sailings.csv` and renders it into `timetable.html`.
- The ferry office exports that CSV once each night.
- No column in the CSV marks a sailing as cancelled. The app has no warning code.

This creates a problem the site cannot solve by itself. The site only knows what the CSV tells it. Many cancellations are probably decided on the day, because of weather or a fault. A nightly file cannot carry those in time. So the main question is not how to show the warning. It is where the news of a cancellation comes from, and how fast it must reach the site.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The app is a read-only view of one nightly snapshot. Any warning faster than "tomorrow" needs a second source of data, or a way to update it during the day.
- That source decides most of the build: a new CSV column, an admin form, or a feed from another system.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Tell me if I have any of this wrong.

When a sailing is cancelled today, who at the ferry office knows first, and how do they tell passengers now?
